segments.text: A cat tips off the edge of the couch and starts to fall.
There's nothing to grab, no wall to push against.
But midair, it flips its whole body to land feet-first.
The inner ear instantly senses which way is up.
A cat's spine is flexible enough to twist front and back separately.
It tucks its front legs and stretches its back legs, twisting the front half first.
Then it reverses, tucking the back legs to twist the rest.
So the cat lands on its feet every time.
